name: Villagers Work Their Own Job First
description: Villagers practise their selected job on their own: about three times in four, each time the game chooses what a villager does, a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building first tries that job's own work, at any food level; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, the game chooses exactly as it always has. The one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. What the work is -- which crop, project, patient or study -- is the game's own choice, with its own technology levels and buildings, so nothing starts that the game itself would not allow. As in the game, a villager goes to their job on their own only above skill 5 -- in every game: in A New Home the game sent them from skill 2, and now waits for 6 as the other games do. Researchers never take the place of a farming attempt, and Parenting is left to the game and the Birth Control patches. **This patch never sends a builder to start a project nobody was ever dropped on; it only puts builders first to carry on work that was started**. Builders are always put first; only the three puzzle chores the Building work could start on its own are left out of the work this patch sends them to while that puzzle is unsolved and nobody has started it -- clearing the stream until The Stream is solved, fixing the piers and clearing the rubble until someone has worked on them -- and every other building job goes on. Once The Stream is solved, keeping it clear counts as building practice. Healers heal the sick, or study medicine once the Hospital has been built. **This patch also turns off the game's "untrained" mark.** In the stock game a villager who has never been dropped on a job does no work on their own at all, however skilled (a child who grew up with skills, for example, just stands around at 14). With this patch every adult 14 or older works on their own as in Virtual Villagers 1-3: the game picks their best skill (or their checked job most of the time) and goes to it only above skill 5, and then only (skill + 40) times in 100, so a skilled villager works often and a beginner still idles. Mating is never put first and stays under the game and the Birth Control patches. The mark is kept in the save, so without this patch the game behaves as it always has. An untrained villager's building work follows the same puzzle rule (above). In catch-up a farmer may also make the fruit trip, "Attempting to retrieve fruit", once the Cooking Pit is restored, as they do while you play. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the Origins-exclusive base appends does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.
behavior_changes: Whenever the adult scheduler (or the catch-up worker's pick dispatch, 0x465827 returning to 0x46582C) asks the work dispatcher to start a job, for a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building (Farming 0, Parenting 1, Healing 2, Research 3, Building 4), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the caller sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the caller's own request runs unchanged. Parenting is never put first, and a request for Parenting (the game's own embrace attempt) is never displaced: it runs unchanged. Research never displaces a Farming request.

About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler and once per run of the catch-up worker (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the caller's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game.

Builders never start a project nobody was dropped on: a builder is always put first; in the Building dispatches this companion causes (a builder put first, or an untrained villager's request run with the mark lifted) the Building case's three puzzle options are left out only while that puzzle is unsolved and unstarted (the owner, 2026-11-19: a solved puzzle's work is never blocked; only an unsolved puzzle's auto-start stays drop-only, for that option alone): option 5, the stream (added at 0x463DD1), until The Stream (project 1) is solved; option 6, the piers (0x463E1C), while 0x421570 on 0x4D86A8 is 0; option 7, the rubble (0x463E3E), while [0x4D8A8C] is 0. Builders Fix Huts When Idle never puts option 6 back then either (VvfpWorkFirstPuzzleBlocked). Its construction only continues projects above 0%.
Only above skill 5 (the owner, 2026-11-18): a villager is never put first while their skill in that job is 5 or less, as every game's job picker never sends them (its own gate, cmp esi, 5).

Untrained mark off (the owner, 2026-11-19): every new villager starts with [record+0x1C54] = 1 (0x45F534), and the dispatcher refuses every job while it is 1 (0x4639D2) -- its only gate; the scheduler's and worker's assigned-site tests (0x46597F, 0x4657C9) and the end-of-action reset (0x45E6DB) treat 1 as nothing assigned. Every request of the scheduler (returns 0x4659D2, 0x465A17, 0x465A2A) and of the catch-up worker (0x46582C, and the low-food Farming dispatch 0x46580F) is dispatched with the mark set to 0 for that call and put back to 1 afterwards if it is still 0 (a refusal inside the call writes 0); the job is the stock picker's (0x461CC0: above skill 5, then (skill + 40)%), Parenting only when it picks it. A Building request run this way follows the puzzle rule above.
At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the sites below at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing.

A villager with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose; the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and a villager with no selected job are untouched.
Parenting (job 1) is never put first, and the catch-up worker's Parenting pick (its 5% conception attempt) is not touched: births stay under the Birth Control patches.

What the work does -- which crop, project, hut, patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice, with its technology levels and buildings; the Farming cases start no tool or sack job (those stay drop-only) and no puzzle work.

In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46580A: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) never puts anyone's own job first, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game; the hook only ignores the untrained mark for it.
Nothing is written to the save or any file. The only record write is the untrained mark, lifted for one dispatch and put back, so the save keeps it.

runtime_detours.routine: the work dispatcher's entry, acting only for the adult scheduler's calls (returns 0x4659D2, 0x465A17, 0x465A2A) and the catch-up worker's pick dispatch (0x46582C); for the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46580F) it only ignores the untrained mark
the Farming case's catch-up test before the fruit trip (cmp byte [game+0x171A4], bl; jne): in catch-up a villager whose selected job is Farming is offered the fruit trip on the decision's roll
the Building case adding option 5, the stream: left out of a Building dispatch this companion causes until The Stream (project 1) is solved
the Building case adding option 6, the piers: left out of a Building dispatch this companion causes while nobody has worked on them (0x421570 on 0x4D86A8 is 0)
the Building case adding option 7, the rubble: left out of a Building dispatch this companion causes while nobody has worked on it ([0x4D8A8C] is 0)
